name: Tracker export row readers: rows to 750 levels read, anything unreadable refuses
summary: The three readers of a project's tracker export rows parse them with the row bound of kittrial-5bb.141 (record_json.loads_rows, ROW_NESTING_MAX 750), not the 64-level comment guard: endpoint.tracker_actors (behind the worker-credential name rule at use and at issue), admin.py credential_actors, and admin.py project_actor_names (adopt-actor). Rows nested up to 750 levels parse normally and their own author, assignee and comment names count; a row nested 65 levels, which the comment guard refused whole, reads. ANY row that cannot be parsed -- unparseable, deeper than 750, a line cut short, a 5,000-digit number -- refuses the read as a whole, exactly as a bd that exits nonzero or an export without the merge slot: an unreadable row may be the row that holds the name, and a name the tracker might hold must not become issuable or writable through a worker credential. A marked row never counts as the merge slot. In the credential-actors listing such a project reads tracker_rows null with the unreadable row ids named; adopt-actor refuses as a tracker that could not be read. An export cut at U+0085 refuses the same way until kittrial-5bb.239 lands.
